title: The Case of the Wet Page
story: A book page is wet. A cup sat on the book. The cup was full. Max read it on the rug. He had no cup. The wet spot is round.
question: What made the page wet?

suspects.why: it sat on the book and it was full

answer: The cup made the page wet.
explain: The wet spot is round like a cup. Because the full cup sat on the book, it made the page wet.

debate.story: A book page is wet. A full cup sat on the book. Max had juice on his hands. He read it outside in the rain. The wet mark is a round ring.
debate.question: What made the page wet? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a full cup on the book
he read it outside in the rain

evidence: “A full cup sat on the book.”
arguments.against: “He read it outside in the rain.”
“The wet mark is a round ring.”

evidence: “He read it outside in the rain.”
arguments.against: “A full cup sat on the book.”

debate.note: A round spot is the shape a cup makes. Draw a cup bottom on paper and let the children see the circle.

title: The Case of the Soft Chips
story: Tam's chips went soft. His bag was open. Air makes chips soft. Jo's bag was shut. Jo's chips are crisp. No one spilled water. Tam shut it next time.
question: Why did the chips go soft?
answer: The open bag let air in.
explain: Jo's bag was shut and her chips are crisp. Because Tam's bag was open, air got in and made the chips soft.

debate.story: Tam's chips went soft. His bag was open. Air makes chips soft. Jo held the bag at play time. A wet cup sat next to it.
debate.question: Why did the chips go soft? Show the words.

suspects.why: an open bag, and air makes chips soft
held the bag at play time
a wet cup next to it

arguments.against: “Jo held the bag at play time.”

evidence: “Jo held the bag at play time.”
“A wet cup sat next to it.”

debate.note: Soft is not wet. Ask the class to feel the difference, and ask what water would have done to the chips.

title: The Case of the Dull Pencil
story: Ann's pencil will not write. The tip is flat. She did not sharpen it. Her other pencil is sharp. The paper is fine. A flat tip makes no line. She sharpened it.
question: Why will the pencil not write?

suspects.why: a flat tip makes no line

answer: The flat tip made no line.
clears: A bad pencil: “Her other pencil is sharp.”
explain: She sharpened it and it wrote. Because the tip was flat, the pencil could not make a line.

debate.story: Ann's pencil will not write. The tip is flat. A flat tip makes no line. The pencil came from a new box. The paper is shiny and slick.
debate.question: Why will the pencil not write? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a flat tip, which makes no line
a pencil from a new box

evidence: “The pencil came from a new box.”

debate.note: Try the pencil on two kinds of paper. That one test answers the whole case in a minute.

title: The Case of the Bitten Apple
story: An apple has a bite. The bite is small. A mouse makes small bites. Sam did not eat it. The cat was outside. Mouse tracks are by the box.
question: Who bit the apple?
answer: A mouse bit the apple.
explain: Mouse tracks are by the box. Because a mouse makes small bites, a mouse bit the apple.

debate.story: An apple has a bite. The bite is small. A mouse makes small bites. Tracks are by the box. Sam sat by the box. The cat came in at nine.
debate.question: Who took a bite? Show the words.

suspects.why: small bites, and a mouse makes small bites

debate.note: Hold up a hand and ask how big Sam's bite would be. Small is the word that matters here.

title: The Case of the Soft Tire
story: Lu's bike tire is soft. A tack is in the tire. Air comes out of a hole. The other tire is hard. Lu did not fall. Her dad pulled the tack out.
question: Why is the tire soft?

suspects.why: a tack is in the tire

answer: A tack made a hole in the tire.
clears: A bad bike: “The other tire is hard.”
explain: Her dad pulled the tack out. Because a tack made a hole, the air came out and the tire went soft.

debate.story: Lu's bike tire is soft. A tack is in the tire. Air comes out of a hole. Lu fell on Friday. The bike is three years old.
debate.question: Why is the tire soft? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a tack in the tire, where air comes out

debate.note: The tack is still in the tire. Ask the class what they would do first, and somebody will want to pull it out.

title: The Case of the Foggy Tank
story: The tank water looks foggy. The class fed the fish a lot. Old food makes water foggy. The filter is clean. No one touched the tank. Less food made it clear.
question: Why did the water look foggy?
answer: Too much food made the water foggy.
proof: “The class fed the fish a lot.”
clears: Touching it: “No one touched the tank.”
explain: Less food made it clear. Because the class fed the fish a lot, the old food made the water foggy.

debate.story: The tank water looks foggy. The class fed the fish a lot. Old food makes water foggy. The filter stopped on Monday. Two hands went in the tank.
debate.question: Why is the water foggy? Show the words.

suspects.why: a lot of food, and old food makes water foggy
a filter that stopped on Monday

evidence: “The class fed the fish a lot.”

arguments.against: “The class fed the fish a lot.”

debate.note: A filter cleans and food dirties. Ask which one stopped and which one went up, and whether both could be true.

title: The Case of the Squeak
story: A squeak came from the door. The hinge is dry. A dry hinge squeaks. The window was shut. No mouse was seen. The door swung open. Oil stopped the squeak.
question: What made the squeak?
answer: The dry hinge made the squeak.
explain: Oil stopped the squeak. Because the hinge was dry, it squeaked when the door swung open.

debate.story: A squeak came from the door. The hinge is dry. A dry hinge squeaks. The window slides open there. A mouse was seen by the door.
debate.question: What is squeaking? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a dry hinge, and a dry hinge squeaks
a window that slides open there
a mouse seen by the door

arguments.against: “A mouse was seen by the door.”

evidence: “A mouse was seen by the door.”

debate.note: Open the classroom door slowly and listen. A squeak you can make again is a squeak you can explain.

title: The Case of the Lost Leaves
story: The leaf pile is gone. The wind blew hard. Wind moves light leaves. The gate was shut. No one raked them. Leaves are by the fence now.
question: What moved the leaves?
answer: The wind blew the leaves away.
explain: Leaves are by the fence now. Because the wind blew hard, it moved the light leaves.

debate.story: The leaf pile is gone. The wind blew hard. Wind moves light leaves. A rake stands by the shed. The yard gate stood open all night long.
debate.question: Where did the leaves go? Show the words.

suspects.why: hard wind, and wind moves light leaves
a rake standing by the shed

evidence: “The yard gate stood open all night long.”

debate.note: Ask where the leaves are now. Nobody has looked, and a five-year-old will want to go and see.

title: The Case of the Squishy Pumpkin
story: The pumpkin feels squishy. It sat by the heater. Heat makes a pumpkin soft. No one dropped it. No bug holes are in it. The cool one is hard.
question: Why is the pumpkin squishy?

suspects.why: no bug holes are in it

answer: The heater made the pumpkin soft.
clears: Bugs: “No bug holes are in it.”
explain: The cool one is hard. Because this pumpkin sat by the heater, the heat made it squishy.

debate.story: The pumpkin feels squishy. It sat by the heater. Heat makes a pumpkin soft. It rolled off the shelf. A small hole is in the side.
debate.question: Why is the pumpkin squishy? Point to the words.

suspects.why: sat by the heater, and heat makes it soft
a small hole in the side

evidence: “A small hole is in the side.”

debate.note: Squishy all over or squishy in one place? The case does not say, and that is a good thing to notice.

title: The Case of the Paw Prints
story: Paw prints cross the floor. They have four toes. A cat has four toes. The class cat was out. Shoes make flat prints. The prints go to the door.
question: Who left the paw prints?

suspects.why: a cat has four toes and the cat was out

answer: The class cat left the prints.
explain: The prints have four toes. Because the class cat was out, the cat walked across the floor.

debate.story: Paw prints cross the floor. Each print shows four toes. A cat has four toes. A dog has four toes too. The mop was used at ten.
debate.question: Who left the prints? Show the words.

suspects.why: four toes, and a cat has four
a dog has four toes too

debate.note: Four toes used to be the answer. Now two animals have four toes, so it is only half an answer.

title: The Case of the Lost Hat
story: Ben's hat is gone. He wore it on the bus. He took it off there. The driver found a hat. His mom checked his room. The hat was not home.
question: Where is the hat?

suspects.why: he wore it on the bus

answer: The hat was on the bus.
clears: At home: “His mom checked his room.”
At school: “He wore it on the bus.”
explain: The driver found a hat. Because Ben took his hat off on the bus, it stayed there.

debate.story: Ben's hat is gone. Ben had it on the bus. The driver found a hat. Two boys have the same hat. His mom did not look in the car.
debate.question: Where is the hat? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a car his mom did not look in
two boys with the same hat

evidence: “His mom did not look in the car.”

debate.note: A hat is not his hat. Ask how Ben could tell, and somebody will say to look for his name.

title: The Case of the Fallen Cup
story: The class cup fell down. The shelf has one loose nail. A loose nail tips a shelf. No one pushed it. The cup is not broken. A new nail fixed it.
question: Why did the cup fall?

suspects.why: a loose nail tips a shelf

answer: A loose nail tipped the shelf.
explain: A new nail fixed it. Because the shelf had a loose nail, it tipped and the cup fell.

debate.story: The class cup fell down. The shelf has one loose nail. A loose nail tips a shelf. The door bangs that wall. The cup has a small chip.
debate.question: Why did the cup fall? Show the words.

suspects.why: a loose nail, which tips a shelf
a door that bangs that wall
a small chip on the cup

debate.note: Did the chip make it fall, or did the fall make the chip? That question is worth asking out loud.

title: The Case of the Cold Corn
story: The corn went cold fast. The bowl came from the fridge. A cold bowl takes heat. The pot was still hot. No window was open. A warm bowl kept it hot.
question: Why did the corn go cold?
answer: The cold bowl took the heat.
clears: The pot: “The pot was still hot.”
explain: A warm bowl kept it hot. Because the bowl came from the fridge, it took the heat from the corn.

debate.story: The corn went cold fast. The bowl came from the fridge. A cold bowl takes heat. The pot sat off the heat. The window by the table is open.
debate.question: Why did the corn go cold? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a bowl from the fridge, which takes heat
a pot sitting off the heat
an open window by the table

arguments.against: “The window by the table is open.”

evidence: “The window by the table is open.”

debate.note: Three cold things and one bowl of corn. Count them on fingers with the class.

title: The Case of the Missing Frosting
story: Six cupcakes have no frosting. Frosting is on the floor. A dog was in the room. Dogs like sweet things. No child was near. Paw prints are on the mat.
question: Who took the frosting?

suspects.why: paw prints are on the mat

answer: A dog ate the frosting.
clears: A bug: “Paw prints are on the mat.”
explain: Paw prints are on the mat. Because a dog was in the room and dogs like sweet things, the dog licked the frosting off.

debate.story: Six cupcakes have no frosting. Frosting is on the floor. Paw marks show on the mat. Dogs like sweet things. A child sat by the tray. Ants are on the floor too.
debate.question: Who took the frosting? Show the words.

suspects.why: paw prints, and dogs like sweet things
a child sitting by the tray

debate.note: The frosting is on the floor, so somebody knocked it rather than ate it. Ants came after.

title: The Case of the Wet Mitten
story: One mitten is wet. Kim made a snowball. She used that hand. Her other hand was in her coat. Snow melts into a mitten. Both dried on the heater.
question: Why is one mitten wet?

suspects.why: her other hand was in her coat

answer: The snowball made the mitten wet.
clears: The heater: “Both dried on the heater.”
Rain: “Her other hand was in her coat.”
explain: Her other hand stayed in her coat. Because Kim made a snowball with one hand, snow melted into that mitten.

debate.story: One mitten is wet. Kim made a snowball. She used that hand. Snow melts into a mitten. That mitten hung on the heater. It rained on the way home.
debate.question: Why is one mitten wet? Point to the words.

suspects.why: made a snowball with that hand
that mitten hung on the heater

debate.note: Rain falls on both hands. Only one mitten is wet. Let the class say why that matters.

title: The Case of the Fallen Candy
story: Candy fell off the house. The class used soft frosting. Soft frosting does not dry. No one bumped it. The walls still stand. Hard icing held the rest.
question: Why did the candy fall off?
answer: The soft frosting did not hold.
explain: Hard icing held the rest. Because the class used soft frosting, it never dried and the candy fell off.

debate.story: Candy fell off the house. The class used soft frosting. Soft frosting does not dry. The table was bumped at lunch. The roof wall leans over.
debate.question: Why did the candy fall? Show the words.

suspects.why: soft frosting, which does not dry
a roof wall that leans over

debate.note: Hard frosting holds candy on a leaning wall. Soft frosting does not hold it on a straight one.

title: The Case of the Dark Lamp
story: The class lamp will not light. The plug is on the floor. A plug must be in the wall. The bulb is new. The switch is on. It lit up when plugged in.
question: Why will the lamp not light?

suspects.why: a plug must be in the wall

answer: The plug was not in the wall.
proof: “A plug must be in the wall.”
clears: A dead bulb: “The bulb is new.”
explain: It lit up when plugged in. Because the plug was on the floor, the lamp had no power.

debate.story: The class lamp will not light. The plug is on the floor. A plug must be in the wall. The bulb is black inside. The switch moves but feels loose.
debate.question: Why will the lamp not light? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a plug on the floor, not in the wall

evidence: “A plug must be in the wall.”

arguments.against: “A plug must be in the wall.”

debate.note: Three things are wrong with one lamp. Ask which one they would fix first and why that one.

title: The Case of the Quiet Clock
story: The class clock stopped. The back has no battery. A clock needs a battery. The hands are not bent. No one dropped it. A new battery started it.
question: Why did the clock stop?
answer: The clock had no battery.
clears: Bent hands: “The hands are not bent.”
explain: A new battery started it. Because the back had no battery, the clock could not run.

debate.story: The class clock stopped. It stopped at three. The back has no battery. A clock needs a battery. One hand is bent a bit. The clock fell last week.
debate.question: Why did the clock stop? Show the words.

suspects.why: no battery, and a clock needs one

debate.note: A fall can bend a hand and knock a battery out. Two of these answers might be one answer.

title: The Case of the Shrinking Snowman
story: The snowman got small. The sun was out all day. Sun melts snow. Water sits all around it. No one pushed it. The yard gate was locked.
question: Why did the snowman get small?
answer: The sun melted the snowman.
clears: A dog: “The yard gate was locked.”
explain: Water sits all around it. Because the sun was out all day, it melted the snow.

debate.story: The snowman got small. The sun was out all day. Sun melts snow. Water sits all around it. Boot marks are by it. The gate was open.
debate.question: Why did the snowman get small? Point to the words.

suspects.why: sun all day, and sun melts snow

debate.note: The water all around it is the snow. Say that out loud and let them work out where it went.

title: The Case of the Empty Dish
story: The bird dish is empty. A squirrel sat on it. Squirrels eat bird seed. No seed is on the ground. Birds eat a little. The class filled it again.
question: Who ate the seed?

suspects.why: no seed is on the ground

answer: A squirrel ate the seed.
clears: A hole: “No seed is on the ground.”
explain: No seed is on the ground. Because a squirrel sat on the dish and squirrels eat bird seed, it ate the seed.

debate.story: The bird dish is empty. A squirrel sat on it. Squirrels eat bird seed. Seed lies on the ground below. Ten small birds came by all day.
debate.question: Where did the seed go? Show the words.

suspects.why: a squirrel on it, and squirrels eat seed
seed lying on the ground below

evidence: “Ten small birds came by all day.”

debate.note: Seed on the ground is seed that nobody ate. Ask whether the dish is empty because of eating or spilling.

title: The Case of the Cold Cup
story: The cocoa went cold. The cup sat by the window. The window was open. Cold air cools a drink. The pot was hot. It sat for one minute. A shut window kept it warm.
question: Why did the cocoa go cold?
answer: Cold air from the window cooled the cocoa.
clears: Sitting too long: “It sat for one minute.”
explain: A shut window kept the next cup warm. Because the window was open, cold air cooled the drink.

debate.story: The cocoa went cold. The cup sat by the window. The window was open. Cold air cools a drink. The pot sat off the stove. The cup waited ten minutes.
debate.question: Why did the cocoa go cold? Point to the words.

suspects.why: an open window, and cold air cools a drink
a pot sitting off the stove

debate.note: Ten minutes is a long time for a drink. Count it on the class clock and watch them change their minds.

title: The Case of the Red Hands
story: Pat has red hands. The red paint jar is open. Paint was on the brush. Pat made a red card. No one else used red. Soap washed it off.
question: Why are Pat's hands red?
answer: The red paint made Pat's hands red.
clears: Somebody else: “No one else used red.”
A crayon: “Paint was on the brush.”
explain: Soap washed it off. Because the red paint jar was open and Pat made a red card, the paint got on Pat's hands.

debate.story: Pat has red hands. The red paint jar is open. Pat made a red card. Jo used the red jar first. A red crayon is broken on the desk.
debate.question: What made Pat's hands red? Show the words.

suspects.why: an open paint jar, and a red card made
Jo used the red jar first
a broken red crayon on the desk

arguments.against: “A red crayon is broken on the desk.”

evidence: “A red crayon is broken on the desk.”

debate.note: Paint and crayon look different on a hand. Ask which one washes off, and try it.

title: The Case of the Quiet Cup
story: The cup made no bubbles. There was no soda in it. Soda makes the bubbles. The vinegar was new. The cup had no crack. Soda made it bubble.
question: Why were there no bubbles?
answer: There was no soda in the cup.
clears: A cracked cup: “The cup had no crack.”
explain: Soda made it bubble when they put some in. Because there was no soda in the cup, nothing bubbled.

debate.story: The cup made no bubbles. There was no soda in it. Soda makes the bubbles. The vinegar jar sat open all year. The cup has a thin crack.
debate.question: Why were there no bubbles? Point to the words.

suspects.why: no soda, and soda makes the bubbles
a thin crack in the cup

arguments.against: “The vinegar jar sat open all year.”

evidence: “The vinegar jar sat open all year.”

debate.note: No bubbles at all is different from a few bubbles. Ask the class which answer gives none.

title: The Case of the Bent Crown
story: The paper crown is bent. It was under a big box. A box bends paper. No one sat on it. The crown is not torn. A flat shelf keeps it straight.
question: What bent the crown?
answer: The big box bent the crown.
clears: Sitting on it: “No one sat on it.”
A tear: “The crown is not torn.”
explain: A flat shelf keeps it straight. Because the crown was under a big box, the box bent the paper.

debate.story: The paper crown is bent. It was under a big box. A box bends paper. Sam sat on that chair. A small tear is on one side.
debate.question: What bent the crown? Show the words.

suspects.why: under a big box, and a box bends paper
a small tear on one side

evidence: “A small tear is on one side.”

debate.note: Bent and torn are two different words. Ask which one the crown is, and whether it is both.

title: The Case of the Soft Note
story: One note sounds soft. A sock is in the piano. A sock makes a note soft. The key goes down fine. No one spilled water. The sock came out.
question: Why does one note sound soft?

suspects.why: a sock makes a note soft

answer: A sock in the piano made the note soft.
clears: A stuck key: “The key goes down fine.”
explain: The sock came out and the note was loud again. Because a sock was in the piano, it made that note soft.

debate.story: One note sounds soft. A sock is in the piano. A sock makes a note soft. That key goes down slowly. A cup spilled on the lid.
debate.question: Why is one note soft? Point to the words.

suspects.why: a sock inside, which makes a note soft
a key that goes down slowly
a cup spilled on the lid

debate.note: Take the sock out and press the key. That is the whole answer and it takes ten seconds.

title: The Case of the Kite in the Tree
story: The kite is in a tree. The string broke. A thin string breaks. The kite has no rips. No one let go. A new string held fine.
question: How did the kite get in the tree?
answer: The thin string broke.
clears: A rip: “The kite has no rips.”
explain: A new string held fine. Because the string was thin, it broke and the kite blew into the tree.

debate.story: The kite is in a tree. The string broke. A thin string breaks. The wind blew hard. Ana's hand was cold. A small rip is near the tail.
debate.question: Why is the kite in the tree? Show the words.

suspects.why: a small rip near the tail

evidence: “A small rip is near the tail.”

debate.note: A broken string and a let-go string look different at the end. Ask what the end of Ana's string looks like.

title: The Case of the Sad Plant
story: The plant leans way over. It sits by one window. Plants lean to the light. The pot has water. The soil is good. A turn made it straight.
question: Why does the plant lean?
answer: The plant leans to the light.
explain: A turn made it straight. Because the plant sits by one window, it leans toward the light.

debate.story: The plant leans way over. It sits by one window. Plants lean to the light. The pot is dry on top. The soil came from the yard.
debate.question: Why does the plant lean? Point to the words.

suspects.why: one window, and plants lean to the light

debate.note: A thirsty plant droops down. This one leans sideways. Show both with your arm.

title: The Case of the Wet Mat
story: The door mat is wet. It rained all morning. Boots bring in water. The sink is far away. No cup was spilled. A dry mat went down.
question: Why is the mat wet?
answer: Wet boots made the mat wet.
clears: The sink: “The sink is far away.”
explain: It rained all morning. Because boots bring in water, the mat by the door got wet.

debate.story: The door mat is wet. It rained all morning. Boots bring in water. The sink is right by the door. A cup lies on its side.
debate.question: Why is the mat wet? Show the words.

suspects.why: rain all morning, and boots bring in water
a sink right by the door
a cup lying on its side

arguments.against: “The sink is right by the door.”

evidence: “The sink is right by the door.”

debate.note: Wet all over or wet in one spot? Go and look at the mat, and the class will tell you.

title: The Case of the Dug Hole
story: A hole is in the dirt. Paw prints are by it. A dog digs holes. No one used a shovel. The seeds are still there. The fence has a gap.
question: Who dug the hole?
answer: A dog dug the hole.
clears: A shovel: “No one used a shovel.”
A bird: “The seeds are still there.”
explain: The fence has a gap. Because paw prints are by the hole and dogs dig holes, a dog came in and dug.

debate.story: A hole is in the dirt. Paw prints are by it. A dog digs holes. A shovel lies on the grass. A bird pecked there all week.
debate.question: Who dug the hole? Point to the words.

suspects.why: paw prints, and a dog digs holes
a shovel lying on the grass
a bird pecking there all week

debate.note: A shovel makes a straight edge and paws make a messy one. Look at the hole before choosing.

title: The Case of the New Birds
story: The nest has no eggs. Three small birds sit near. Eggs turn into birds. No shells are on the path. No cat came by. The birds can fly now.
question: What happened to the eggs?

suspects.why: no shells are on the path

answer: The eggs turned into birds.
clears: Falling: “No shells are on the path.”
explain: The birds can fly now. Because three small birds sit near the nest, the eggs hatched.

debate.story: The nest has no eggs. Three small birds sit near. Eggs turn into birds. A cat sat under the tree. The nest leans to one side.
debate.question: Where did the eggs go? Show the words.

suspects.why: three small birds near, and eggs turn into birds
a nest that leans to one side

debate.note: Count the eggs and count the birds. Three and three is the best answer a five-year-old can give.

title: The Case of the Paper on the Grass
story: Paper is on the grass. The bin has no lid. Wind lifts loose paper. The bin is not full. No one threw it. A lid stopped the mess.
question: How did the paper get on the grass?
answer: Wind lifted paper out of the bin.
clears: A full bin: “The bin is not full.”
explain: A lid stopped the mess. Because the bin had no lid, the wind lifted the paper out.

debate.story: Paper is on the grass. The bin has no lid. Wind lifts loose paper. The bin is full to the top. Two children ate lunch there.
debate.question: Why is paper on the grass? Point to the words.

suspects.why: no lid, and wind lifts loose paper

suspects.who: 🗑️ A bin full to the top
suspects.why: a bin full to the top
two children who ate lunch there

arguments.against: “The bin is full to the top.”

evidence: “The bin is full to the top.”

debate.note: A full bin and no lid work together. Ask whether emptying the bin would be enough on a windy day.

title: The Case of the Blurry Face
story: The photo face is blurry. Max moved when it clicked. Moving makes a blurry photo. The lens is clean. The light was good. The next one is clear.
question: Why is the face blurry?
answer: Max moved when the camera clicked.
clears: A dirty lens: “The lens is clean.”
explain: The next one is clear. Because Max moved when it clicked, that photo came out blurry.

debate.story: The photo face is blurry. Max moved when it clicked. Moving makes a blurry photo. The lens has a smudge. The room was dim that day.
debate.question: Why is the photo blurry? Show the words.

suspects.why: moved when it clicked, and moving blurs a photo

debate.note: Only the face is blurry. Ask what the rest of the photo looks like, because nobody has said.

title: The Case of the Dry Seed
story: The seed did not grow. The cup has no water. Seeds need water to grow. The seed was new. The sun hit the cup. Water made it sprout.
question: Why did the seed not grow?
answer: The seed had no water.
clears: A bad seed: “The seed was new.”
No sun: “The sun hit the cup.”
explain: Water made it sprout. Because the cup had no water, the seed could not grow.

debate.story: The seed did not grow. The cup has no water. Seeds need water to grow. The seed came from an old jar. The cup sat in a dark box.
debate.question: Why did the seed not grow? Point to the words.

suspects.why: no water, and seeds need water
a seed from an old jar
a cup in a dark box

arguments.against: “The seed came from an old jar.”

evidence: “The seed came from an old jar.”
“The cup sat in a dark box.”

debate.note: Plant four more seeds and change one thing each time. That is a whole week of science from six sentences.

title: The Case of the Soup Cup
story: The ice cream is soup. The cup sat in the sun. Sun melts ice cream. The lid was on tight. It was cold at first. The shade cup is firm.
question: Why did the ice cream melt?
answer: The sun melted the ice cream.
clears: A bad lid: “The lid was on tight.”
Warm milk: “It was cold at first.”
explain: The shade cup is firm. Because this cup sat in the sun, the sun melted it.

debate.story: The ice cream is soup. The cup sat in the sun. Sun melts ice cream. The lid was not pushed down. The cup was warm when it was filled. The shade cup is firm.
debate.question: Why is the ice cream soup? Show the words.

suspects.why: sat in the sun, and sun melts ice cream
a cup that was warm when filled

evidence: “The cup was warm when it was filled.”

debate.note: The shade cup is the one to keep pointing at. Same ice cream, same lid, no sun, still firm.

title: The Case of the Lost Ribbon
story: Mia cannot find her ribbon. Her bag has a hole. Things fall through a hole. She did not give it away. No one took it. The ribbon was under her desk.
question: Where did the ribbon go?

suspects.why: she did not give it away

answer: The ribbon fell through the hole in her bag.
clears: Giving it away: “She did not give it away.”
Somebody taking it: “No one took it.”
explain: The ribbon was under her desk. Because her bag has a hole, the ribbon fell through it.

debate.story: Mia cannot find her ribbon. Her bag has a hole. Things fall through a hole. She lent it to Ann. Two ribbons in the class look the same.
debate.question: Where is the ribbon? Point to the words.

suspects.why: two ribbons that look the same

evidence: “Two ribbons in the class look the same.”

debate.note: Lost is not the only way a thing goes missing. Sometimes you gave it to somebody and forgot.

title: The Case of the Flat Balloon
story: The balloon is flat. The knot came undone. Air goes out an open knot. No pin was near. No one sat on it. A new knot held the air.
question: Why did the balloon go flat?

suspects.why: air goes out an open knot

answer: The knot came undone and the air went out.
clears: Sitting on it: “No one sat on it.”
explain: A new knot held the air. Because the knot came undone, the air went out of the balloon.

debate.story: The balloon is flat. The knot came undone. Air goes out an open knot. A pin is on the floor. It was under a coat all night.
debate.question: Why is the balloon flat? Show the words.

evidence: “It was under a coat all night.”

debate.note: A pin pops a balloon with a bang. A flat balloon went down quietly. Ask if anybody heard anything.
